Identification of cost-effective material for sulfur TES construction The objective was to determine cost-effective materials that meet the vessel cost target (C ) of 26 $/kWh established in Task 2, using information from the corrosion vessel,target rate and mechanical durability testing data. The sulfur TES vessel cost was computed using the cost model described in Task 5, which incorporates the measured corrosion rate and weld strength reduction factor to determine required vessel wall thickness for any given system lifetime per ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel code (BPVC) [29]. The sulfur TES vessel cost is plotted as a function of storage capacity in Figure 17. The cost values are plotted for vessel made of SS 304 and SS 316 alloy for molten sulfur thermally cycling between 300-200 oC (∆T = 100 oC e.g. for process heat temperature requirement of 200 oC) and 300-150 oC (∆T = 150 oC e.g. for process heat temperature requirement of 140 oC). The result shows that both SS-316 and SS-304 satisfies C vessel, of 26 $/kWh for storage capacities above 500 MWh. The cost of SS-304 vessel target including insulation was calculated to be 16.5 (±5) $/kWh for ∆T =100 oC and 13.5 (±4) $/kWh for ∆T =150 C oC at 500 MWh capacity. The design specifications for the 500 MWh sulfur TES tank with molten sulfur thermally cycling between 210-310 oC (∆T =100 oC) are: tank volume of ~7000 m3 and sulfur mass of ~16000 metric tons.
